name: tor-proxy
epitaph: Routed everything except its own future.
description: A small proxy wrapper around Tor. Worked on the first try, which removed every reason to keep opening it.
cause: solved the problem it was written for

name: audio_for_zumers
epitaph: Nobody's friends ever used it.
description: Self-hosted Telegram bot that turned links into audio for people who refuse to read. Ran for six months on a box that eventually got repurposed.
cause: the box got repurposed

name: SBert-Sociology
epitaph: The model understood society. The author didn't.
description: Using sentence embeddings to cluster open-ended survey answers about sociological problems. The clustering worked; interpreting it was a different degree.
cause: scope exceeded interest

name: Time Machine на kopia
epitaph: Somebody had already built it, and was giving it away.
description: Time Machine for every platform — a friendly face on kopia's backup engine. BlinkDisk had already forked kopia, built exactly that, and given it away, charging only for storage, which this was never going to sell.
cause: BlinkDisk shipped the same fork of kopia, free

name: Build in public
epitaph: A hedge tied to the thing it was hedging.
description: Monetising the making rather than the made: document the process, sell that, and stay paid even if no product lands. The audience for it subscribes to progress, so the hedge only pays out while the thing it was hedging is already working.
cause: the genre pays for numbers, and there were none

name: Гитарный пресет
epitaph: Good, obvious, and four teams got there first.
description: Find the amp and pedal settings for any song, band or genre. Four teams had the same idea; one of them gives the answer away inside the largest database of guitar tabs in the world.
cause: the answer was already free inside the biggest tab site in the world

name: Инди без 18+
epitaph: A cure for thirst, served in an empty glass.
description: A catalogue of indie games with the adult content left out, as an alternative to itch.io. Developers leave a platform because nobody sees their game, and a clean, empty catalogue guarantees that nobody does.
cause: a catalogue with no players is a guaranteed zero

name: Авито для Черногории
epitaph: Nobody had complained. Somebody had assumed.
description: A classifieds site for Montenegro, on the premise that the country had none. It had several. The relocant channels it would have grown from held about 26,000 people, against the 2,200 to 11,000 daily visits the ad model needed.
cause: a market of 26,000 people, needing 11,000 visits a day

name: Заметки для Boox
epitaph: The feature shipped with the device, for nothing.
description: A handwritten notes app for Onyx Boox readers, where lassoing a scribble would link it to another notebook. The stock firmware already does that, free, on the manufacturer's own low-latency pen.
cause: lasso-to-link was already in the free stock firmware

name: Диф с навигацией
epitaph: Everyone wanted it. Nobody had ever paid for it.
description: A diff viewer where ctrl+click jumps to a definition without leaving the diff. A working prototype existed, and so did six live free tools doing the same thing, which is how a category's price gets fixed at zero.
cause: six free competitors had set the category's price at zero

name: cursor-kit
epitaph: One commit long, and it already worked.
description: Custom mouse pointers for macOS screen recordings — an iPadOS-style circle instead of the arrow, animated if you want, with a press reaction that contracts on mouse-down and springs back.
cause: there was nothing to add on day two

name: JustSit
epitaph: Never congratulated anyone. Not even itself.
description: Wallace's ten stages of shamatha, taught slowly. Every plant in its garden is one finished sitting; leave one early and nothing grows, and nothing is said about that either.
cause: it reached iOS and stopped needing anything

name: Graveyard
epitaph: Dug every hole here, then lay down in one.
description: A scrollable cemetery of dead projects. Every grave carries the years it ran, a line for the epitaph and a line for what killed it, and anyone can leave a candle. No server, no database, no build step.
cause: it buried itself to prove the shovel worked

name: craft-readme
epitaph: Wrote the landing page for everything except a second version.
description: A Claude Code skill that rebuilds a README as a landing page and takes the screenshots itself — a hero shot and a GIF over headless Chromium, with the reference detail moved out to a guide.
cause: the skill was the whole product

name: JediNotebook
epitaph: No account, no server, no one to sync with.
description: Projects with tasks, time-boxed into today, this week, or someday. Kept in the browser's own database — no account, no server, nothing to sync.
cause: kept on this device, and stayed there

name: art-window
epitaph: Hung a painting behind every other window.
description: A daily painting on your desktop, always fit to the screen with black borders.
cause: the desktop was already full

name: CtrlClickDiff
epitaph: The prototype worked. The idea beside it had already been filtered.
description: Ctrl+click any symbol in a reviewed diff and its declaration opens in a peek widget, inline. Same tab, same scroll position, resolved by name at the revision under review.
cause: six free tools had fixed the category price at zero

name: karakuli
epitaph: Its paper is still under this yard.
description: Paper, one pen, and colour kept back for the moments that earn it.
cause: finished; it lives in everything it was used for

name: article
epitaph: Told the agents what it looked like. They kept guessing.
description: Agents build interfaces that all look the same, because nothing tells them what your software looks like. Article is that instruction, written down.
cause: written down, and that was the deliverable

name: PapaSheets
epitaph: Shipped to version 1.3, for one site.
description: An offline Android journal for construction work — a date × contractor matrix, photographs on any cell, and an xlsx export. Built for one site and shipped to version 1.3.
cause: the job it logged was finished

name: software-design-lenses
epitaph: Nine ways to look at code. One review.
description: A family of Claude Code skills that analyze a code solution (a snippet/module) or a whole project through the perspectives ("lenses") of John Ousterhout's A Philosophy of Software Design. Each lens reports its findings in a shared schema, so findings compose into a single design-review report.
cause: the lenses were ground, and then set down

name: NomadNotes
epitaph: Wrote on the panel. The firmware already did.
description: A handwriting notes app for Onyx Boox e-ink tablets (validated on a Boox Go 10.3), aiming for the lag-free, paper-like inking feel of a Supernote. The pen writes directly on the e-ink panel via the Onyx SDK's raw-drawing path; finished strokes are persisted so ink survives refreshes.
cause: lasso-to-link shipped free in the stock firmware

name: TheMap
epitaph: A runic language for maps, and no one to read it.
description: Palimpsest — a generative living map, with a runic language for its cards and the laws that govern them written as tablets in the same language.
cause: one commit, and the language stayed private

name: tab-pal
epitaph: Rebuilt after two years, and finished the same day.
description: A cross-platform colour-palette tool — generate, browse, and check palettes — built as one web/desktop/mobile codebase around a pure, perceptually-uniform colour engine. A Coolors-style app, offline-first.
cause: Coolors was already free and already open

name: JewelSort
epitaph: Sorted the jewels. Never sorted a player.
description: A casual tap-cluster-sort puzzle prototype built in LÖVE 11.x. Source PNG images define the level — each opaque pixel becomes a jewel-shaped hole whose target color is the pixel's RGB.
cause: a prototype that reached v0.5 and stopped

name: pixeltui
epitaph: Queued the art. Nobody came back for it.
description: A Textual TUI for queueing pixel-art generation jobs against ComfyUI.
cause: cleaned up for a public release that had no audience
